# What this costs, and whether it fits

**Generated by `scripts/estimate_credit_cost.py` from the real cached schedule. It spends nothing and touches no network.** The reasoning that is not arithmetic lives in `docs/credit_cost.md`, because a finding appended to a regenerated file lasts exactly one re-run.

Regions `us,us2` (2). Every figure is the **pessimistic bound** — every asked-for market returning at every book. Real spend can only come in under it, and is separately capped against the measured running total from `x-requests-last`.

## The season's shape, measured

| Season | Games | D-I v D-I | Non-D-I | Slate days | Mean/day | Median | **Peak day** |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| 2025 | 6,299 | 5,764 | 530 | 152 | 41.4 | 32 | **199** |
| 2026 | 6,318 | 5,752 | 551 | 147 | 43.0 | 35 | **169** |
| 2027 | 1,629 | 1,593 | 36 | 108 | 15.1 | 11 | **59** |

The peak is **200 games in one day**, in season 2023. That is opening Monday: the season's largest slate is its first, not a February Saturday. Every cap below is set against it, because **a cap below the worst slate is a cap that starves it, and a starved fetch and an unquoted market look identical in the reports.**

**The 2027 row is a partial schedule, not a short season.** ESPN fills the calendar in over the autumn; 1,520 of its 1,629 rows still carry a midnight placeholder rather than a tip time. Every projection below uses the completed seasons for shape.

## Live fetching, per day and per season

- Bulk call: **3 featured keys x 2 regions = 6 credits**, whole slate, once per snapshot. On a 200-game day that is 200 games for 6 credits, which is why the featured markets are never asked per event.
- Per event: **48 keys x 2 regions = 96 credits** pessimistic — every ladder, half and prop returning at every book. In practice a low-major Tuesday game returns a handful, and an unquoted market costs nothing.

| Snapshots/day | Peak day (pessimistic) | Peak day (featured only) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 19,206 | 6 |
| 2 | 38,412 | 12 |
| 3 | 57,618 | 18 |

## Buying history

Historical endpoints bill **10x** the live rate. Two provider-documented cut-offs decide what is buyable at all:

- **Featured markets** (`h2h`, `spreads`, `totals`) exist from **2020-11-16** for `basketball_ncaab`.
- **Everything else** — props, halves, every alternate ladder — exists from **2023-05-03**, site-wide. That date falls *after* the 2022-23 season ended, so **the full catalogue is buyable for three seasons and no more**: 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26.

| Tier | Keys | Credits/event | 3 seasons, 1 snapshot | 3 seasons, 2 snapshots |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1-1 | 4 | 80 | 1,379,360 | 2,758,720 |
| 1-2 | 21 | 420 | 7,241,640 | 14,483,280 |
| 1-3 | 51 | 1,020 | 17,586,840 | 35,173,680 |

**Featured markets reach back further.** 32,379 games across seasons 2021-2026 at 60 credits an event is **1,942,740** for one snapshot each — six seasons of moneyline, spread and total, which is the largest priced population any of these four labs has ever had.

## Against the quota

- **Quota remaining: 4,992,714**, read from 
  `x-requests-remaining` on a free `/v4/sports` call, 2026-09-01. Not documentation — the header.
- **Siblings' committed monthly spend: 36,175**
  - `football-betting-lab`: 10,084
  - `nhl-betting-lab`: 26,091
- **Cooper's standing authorisation: 1,500,000 per calendar month** for this lab.

The heaviest thing this lab will ever do in one month is the historical purchase. The full three-season, two-snapshot buy at tier 1-3 is **35,173,680** credits — which is more than one month's authorisation, so it is bought in priority order across months: **core team markets across every season first, then ladders, then props, then futures.** That is Cooper's stated order and it is also the order of decreasing confidence that a market is quoted at all.

Against 4,992,714 remaining and roughly 180,875 committed to the siblings over a five-month college season, there is about **4,811,839** of headroom. The live season at two snapshots a day is a rounding error inside it, and **no live in-season fetch can be starved by the purchase** because the purchase runs under its own cap in its own workflow and the card's fetch checks `x-requests-remaining` against its cap before it starts.

**A starved fetch and an unquoted market look identical.** The NHL lab's probe once reported its own starvation as market absence. Every report in this repository states the cap it ran under and the credits it actually spent, so the two can be told apart.
